Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production transparent medieval strategy-game upgrade sprite sheet. Brand-new art, existing image is STYLE GUIDANCE ONLY: detailed painterly realistic isometric miniature, gray limestone, aged oak, dark iron, selective bronze/gold trim and burgundy banners at late tiers; warm light from upper left, crisp high-detail texture, readable silhouette at small size, muted natural tones. Camera invariant throughout: orthographic isometric three-quarter view at roughly 35 degrees elevation, front and right sides visible, weapon aims diagonally toward lower-right. No people, no text, no numbers, no letters, no grid lines, no outlines, no watermarks, no background scene. Genuine transparent alpha background everywhere around objects and between cells, no painted checkerboard. Every sprite is one entire fully assembled believable object, completely inside its own cell with generous empty gutter, centered horizontally and with bases near the same baseline per row. Small neatly trimmed isometric footings only, no giant scenery or ground slabs.
Primary request: TEN visibly different cumulative upgrade levels of a cannon defense building, arranged in EXACTLY FIVE equal-width columns and TWO equal-height rows, level order LEFT TO RIGHT on top row levels 1–5, then LEFT TO RIGHT bottom row levels 6–10. Canvas wide 5:2 ratio. All cells identical dimensions and no overlaps. Growth is mandatory at EVERY level: first object's width and height about 55% of final, increase around 5% per level. Camera/zoom fixed; physically grow weapon and structure, not equal-sized reframing. Make each adjacent tier obviously distinct with the specified NEW substantial structure.
Tier 1: small single black iron field cannon, simple low oak cradle, two small wooden wheels, compact rectangular timber footing.
Tier 2: larger cannon with reinforced four-wheel carriage and thicker oak side cheeks.
Tier 3: still larger cannon with exposed screw elevation mechanism, iron wheel rims, broad braced timber base.
Tier 4: heavier cannon with larger barrel rings, shielded loading deck, stacked roundshot and winch.
Tier 5: cannon mounted into low gray-stone battery with two flanking masonry piers and timber rear platform.
Tier 6: taller wider stone battery with front crenellated armor and broad steps and heavy cannon.
Tier 7: expanded fortified battery with side ammunition alcove, iron shielding and short burgundy banner.
Tier 8: large bronze siege cannon with thick collar, reinforced recoil rails and side buttresses.
Tier 9: larger armored siege battery with two corner merlons, bronze barrel muzzle, small side companion cannon.
Tier 10: grand massive bronze siege cannon with two smaller side cannons, thick gray-stone bastion, gold-trimmed iron plates, tall rear burgundy banner, enlarged reinforced firing platform.
The 10 cells must depict increasing complexity and increasing physical dimensions in exact listed sequence, never descending or alternating. Do not repeat one silhouette with decoration swaps.
